column1: # denylist.tsv -- the rule table behind guard_path().
#   kind      DENY | ASK | ALLOW | CHILDREN | DENYGLOB | ASKGLOB
#   pattern   absolute path, or ~ for $HOME. DENYGLOB/ASKGLOB use shell case globbing.
#   mindepth  minimum path depth (number of '/' separators) required to match
#   mode      self | children | none   (children = delete contents, keep the directory)
#   reason    shown to the user verbatim when the rule fires
#   - DENY/ASK/ALLOW/CHILDREN are PREFIX rules: match if path == pattern or path starts with pattern/
#   - Longest matching pattern wins. Ties break toward the stronger verdict:
#   - A path matching NO rule is DENIED. Default-deny is the whole point.
#   - ~/.clean-mac-ai/denylist.local.tsv is appended after this file but may only
#     STRENGTHEN rules; ALLOW lines there are ignored so nobody can unprotect /System.
